question.text: The Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund (Cat III) has constituted an Investment Committee (IC) to approve strategy-level decisions. Under SEBI's framework for extending IC decision-making to external members, the Investment Manager must obtain consent for each investment from at least what percentage of external IC members?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Where the IC includes external members and is granted decision-making authority, SEBI requires approval from at least 75% of external members for each investment decision. A waiver of this 75% external-consent rule is available only for specific large-value fund structures (e.g., the INR 70 cr per investor threshold). This protects against hollowed-out IM structures where external members rubber-stamp decisions. **The Trap:** Options A and B understate the threshold. Option D overstates to unanimity which is not required. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the same 75% IC rule. XIX-D tests it with Cat I/II framing — same numerical threshold. XXI-B (PM) does not have an IC rule of this kind. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** If you've onboarded three external ICs for domain expertise (e.g., one each for macro, quant, event), remember ALL three must count toward the 75% — losing one to recusal or unavailability blocks the deal. Budget IC-member back-ups and document recusal procedure in the IC charter.
